    92→        '      "sub_axes": {"abstraction_leverage": 0-100, "indirection_cost": 0-100, "interface_honesty": 0-100, "delegation_density": 0-100, "definition_directness": 0-100, "type_discipline": 0-100}  // required for abstraction_fitness when evidence supports it; all one decimal place\n'
    93→        "    }\n"
    94→        "  },\n"

    98→        '      "score_rationale": "2-3 sentences explaining the score, referencing global anchors"\n'
    99→        "    }  // required for every assessed dimension; do not omit\n"

   107→        '    "suggestion": "concrete fix recommendation",\n'
   108→        '    "confidence": "high|medium|low",\n'
   109→        '    "impact_scope": "local|module|subsystem|codebase",\n'
   110→        '    "fix_scope": "single_edit|multi_file_refactor|architectural_change",\n'
   111→        '    "root_cause_cluster": "optional_cluster_name_when_supported_by_history",\n'
   112→        '    "concern_verdict": "confirmed|dismissed  // for concern signals only",\n'
   113→        '    "concern_fingerprint": "abc123  // required when dismissed; copy from signal fingerprint",\n'
   114→        '    "reasoning": "why dismissed  // optional, for dismissed only"\n'
   115→        "  }],\n"
   116→        '  "retrospective": {\n'
   117→        '    "root_causes": ["optional: concise root-cause hypotheses"],\n'
   118→        '    "likely_symptoms": ["optional: identifiers that look symptom-level"],\n'
   119→        '    "possible_false_positives": ["optional: prior concept keys likely mis-scoped"]\n'
   120→        "  },\n"
   121→        '  "context_updates": {\n'
   122→        '    "<dimension>": {\n'
   123→        '      "add": [{"header": "short label", "description": "why this is the way it is", "settled": true|false, "positive": true|false}],\n'
   124→        '      "remove": ["header of insight to remove"],\n'
   125→        '      "settle": ["header of insight to mark as settled"],\n'
   126→        '      "unsettle": ["header of insight to unsettle"]\n'
   127→        "    }  // omit context_updates entirely if no changes\n"
   128→        "  }\n"
   129→        "}\n"
   130→        + _render_context_update_example()
   131→    )
   132→
   133→def render_batch_prompt(
   134→    *,
   135→    repo_root: Path,
   136→    packet_path: Path,
   137→    batch_index: int,
   138→    batch: dict[str, object],
   139→    policy_block: str = "",
   140→) -> str:
   141→    """Render one subagent prompt for a holistic investigation batch."""
   142→    context = build_batch_context(batch, batch_index)
   143→    dim_prompts = context.dimension_prompts or batch_dimension_prompts(batch)
   144→    dimension_contexts = batch.get("dimension_contexts") if isinstance(batch, dict) else None
   145→    return join_non_empty_sections(
   146→        _render_metadata_block(
   147→            repo_root=repo_root,
   148→            packet_path=packet_path,
   149→            batch_index=batch_index,
   150→            context=context,
   151→        ),
   152→        render_dimension_prompts_block(context.dimensions, dim_prompts),
   153→        policy_block,
   154→        render_scoring_frame(),
   155→        render_dimension_context_block(
   156→            context.dimensions,
   157→            dimension_contexts if isinstance(dimension_contexts, dict) else {},
   158→        ),
   159→        render_scan_evidence_note(),
   160→        render_seed_files_block(context),
   161→        render_historical_focus(batch),
   162→        render_dimension_deferral_context(batch),
   163→        render_mechanical_concern_signals(batch),
   164→        render_judgment_findings_section(batch),
   165→        render_task_requirements(issues_cap=context.issues_cap, dim_set=context.dimension_set),
   166→        render_scope_enums(),
   167→        _render_output_schema(context, batch_index),
   168→    )
   169→
   170→
   171→__all__ = ["render_batch_prompt"]

   133→def render_historical_focus(batch: PromptBatchPayload) -> str:

   135→    if not isinstance(focus, dict):

   137→

   157→    # Group issues by status category

   159→    for entry in issues:

   189→        lines.extend(_render_entry(e) for e in resolved)

   191→    # Any unknown statuses

   229→def _concern_signal_lines(entry: dict[str, object]) -> list[str]:
   230→    """Render one concern signal entry into prompt lines."""
   231→    file = str(entry.get("file", "")).strip() or "(unknown file)"
   232→    concern_type = str(entry.get("type", "")).strip() or "design_concern"
   233→    summary = str(entry.get("summary", "")).strip()

   235→    evidence_raw = entry.get("evidence", [])
   236→    evidence = (
   237→        [str(item).strip() for item in evidence_raw if isinstance(item, str) and item.strip()]
   238→        if isinstance(evidence_raw, list)
   239→        else []
   240→    )
   241→    lines = [f"  - [{concern_type}] {file}"]
   242→    if summary:
   243→        lines.append(f"    summary: {summary}")
   244→    if question:
   245→        lines.append(f"    question: {question}")
   246→    lines.extend(f"    evidence: {snippet}" for snippet in evidence[:2])
   247→    fingerprint = str(entry.get("fingerprint", "")).strip()
   248→    if fingerprint:
   249→        lines.append(f"    fingerprint: {fingerprint}")
   250→    return lines

   260→def _build_concern_summary(valid_signals: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[str]:
   261→    """Build a grouped summary of concern signals by type."""
   262→    by_type: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   263→    for entry in valid_signals:
   264→        concern_type = str(entry.get("type", "")).strip() or "design_concern"
   265→        file = str(entry.get("file", "")).strip() or "(unknown)"
   266→        by_type.setdefault(concern_type, []).append(file)
   267→
   268→    if not by_type:
   269→        return []
   270→
   271→    lines = [f"Overview ({len(valid_signals)} signals):"]
   272→    for concern_type, files in sorted(by_type.items(), key=lambda x: -len(x[1])):
   273→        if len(files) <= 3:
   274→            file_list = ", ".join(files)
   275→            lines.append(f"  {concern_type}: {len(files)} — {file_list}")
   276→        else:
   277→            sample = ", ".join(files[:2])
   278→            lines.append(f"  {concern_type}: {len(files)} — {sample}, ...")
   279→    lines.append("")

   283→def render_mechanical_concern_signals(batch: PromptBatchPayload) -> str:
   284→    """Render mechanically-generated concern hypotheses for this batch."""
   285→    signals = batch.get("concern_signals")
   286→    if not isinstance(signals, list) or not signals:

   288→
   289→    valid_signals = _iter_valid_concern_signals(signals)
   290→    if not valid_signals:

   292→
   293→    lines: list[str] = []
   294→    lines.append("Mechanical concern signals — investigate and adjudicate:")
   295→    lines.extend(_build_concern_summary(valid_signals))
   296→    lines.append("For each concern, read the source code and report your verdict in issues[]:")
   297→    lines.append(

   308→    )
   309→    lines.append("")

   311→    capped_signals = valid_signals[:30]
   312→    for entry in capped_signals:

   318→    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"

   381→        "    - packet/batch data being generated but dropped before prompt execution,\n"
   382→        "    - ranking/triage logic that can starve target-improving work,\n"
   383→        "    - reruns happening before existing open review work is drained.\n"
   384→        "    If found, propose concrete guardrails and where to implement them.\n"
   385→    )
   386→
   387→
   388→def render_package_org_focus(dim_set: set[str]) -> str:
   389→    if "package_organization" not in dim_set:
   390→        return ""
   391→    return (
   392→        "9a. For package_organization, ground scoring in objective structure signals from "
   393→        "`holistic_context.structure` (root_files fan_in/fan_out roles, directory_profiles, "
   394→        "coupling_matrix). Prefer thresholded evidence (for example: fan_in < 5 for root "
   395→        "stragglers, import-affinity > 60%, directories > 10 files with mixed concerns).\n"
   396→        "9b. Suggestions must include a staged reorg plan (target folders, move order, "
   397→        "and import-update/validation commands).\n"
   398→        "9c. Also consult `holistic_context.structure.flat_dir_issues` for directories "
   399→        "flagged as overloaded, fragmented, or thin-wrapper patterns.\n"
   400→    )
   401→
   402→
   403→def render_abstraction_focus(dim_set: set[str]) -> str:
   404→    if "abstraction_fitness" not in dim_set:
   405→        return ""
   406→    return (
   407→        "9d. For abstraction_fitness, use evidence from `holistic_context.abstractions`:\n"
   408→        "  - `delegation_heavy_classes`: classes where most methods forward to an inner "
   409→        "object — entries include class_name, delegate_target, sample_methods, and line number.\n"
   410→        "  - `facade_modules`: re-export-only modules with high re_export_ratio — entries "
   411→        "include samples (re-exported names) and loc.\n"
   412→        "  - `typed_dict_violations`: TypedDict fields accessed via .get()/.setdefault()/.pop() "
   413→        "— entries include typed_dict_name, violation_type, field, and line number.\n"
   414→        "  - `complexity_hotspots`: files where mechanical analysis found extreme parameter "
   415→        "counts, deep nesting, or disconnected responsibility clusters.\n"
   416→        "  Include `delegation_density`, `definition_directness`, and `type_discipline` "
   417→        "alongside existing sub-axes in dimension_notes when evidence supports it.\n"
   418→    )
   419→
   420→
   421→def render_dimension_focus(dim_set: set[str]) -> str:
   422→    return (
   423→        render_package_org_focus(dim_set)
   424→        + render_abstraction_focus(dim_set)
   425→        + render_scan_evidence_focus(dim_set)
   426→        + render_workflow_integrity_focus(dim_set)
   427→    )
   428→
   429→
   430→def explode_to_single_dimension(
   431→    batches: list[PromptBatchPayload],
   432→    dimension_prompts: dict[str, dict[str, object]] | None = None,
   433→) -> list[PromptBatchPayload]:
   434→    """Split multi-dimension batches into one batch per dimension.
   435→
   436→    Preserves seed files and rationale — each exploded batch keeps the same
   437→    file grouping but is scoped to a single dimension. When *dimension_prompts*
   438→    is provided, each exploded batch gets a public ``dimension_prompts`` map
   439→    scoped to its single dimension.
   440→    """
   441→    prompts = dimension_prompts or {}
   442→    result: list[PromptBatchPayload] = []
   443→    for batch in batches:
   444→        dims = batch.get("dimensions", [])
   445→        if not isinstance(dims, list):
   446→            result.append(batch)
   447→            continue
   448→        for dim in dims:
   449→            exploded: PromptBatchPayload = {**batch, "dimensions": [dim]}
   450→            dim_prompt = prompts.get(dim)
   451→            if isinstance(dim_prompt, dict):
   452→                exploded["dimension_prompts"] = {str(dim): dim_prompt}
   453→            result.append(exploded)
   454→    return result
   455→
   456→
   457→def render_dimension_prompts_block(
   458→    dimensions: tuple[str, ...],
   459→    dimension_prompts: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
   460→) -> str:
   461→    """Render inline dimension guidance so the reviewer sees the full rubric."""
   462→    if not dimensions or not dimension_prompts:
   463→        return ""
   464→    lines: list[str] = ["DIMENSION TO EVALUATE:\n"]
   465→    for dim in dimensions:
   466→        prompt = dimension_prompts.get(dim)
   467→        if not isinstance(prompt, dict):
   468→            lines.append(f"## {dim}\n(no rubric available)\n")
   469→            continue
   470→        description = str(prompt.get("description", "")).strip()
   471→        lines.append(f"## {dim}")
   472→        if description:
   473→            lines.append(description)
   474→
   475→        look_for = prompt.get("look_for")
   476→        if isinstance(look_for, list) and look_for:
   477→            lines.append("Look for:")
   478→            for item in look_for:
   479→                lines.append(f"- {item}")
   480→
   481→        skip = prompt.get("skip")
   482→        if isinstance(skip, list) and skip:
   483→            lines.append("Skip:")
   484→            for item in skip:
   485→                lines.append(f"- {item}")
   486→        lines.append("")
   487→    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
   488→
   489→
   490→def render_dimension_context_block(
   491→    dimensions: tuple[str, ...],
   492→    dimension_contexts: dict[str, dict],
   493→) -> str:
   494→    """Render accumulated codebase context for dimensions that have insights.
   495→
   496→    Only surfaces headers in the prompt text — full descriptions are in the
   497→    blind packet's ``dimension_contexts`` section.
   498→    """
   499→    if not dimensions or not dimension_contexts:
   500→        return ""
   501→
   502→    sections: list[str] = []
   503→    for dim in dimensions:
   504→        ctx = dimension_contexts.get(dim)
   505→        if not isinstance(ctx, dict):
   506→            continue
   507→        insights = ctx.get("insights")
   508→        if not isinstance(insights, list) or not insights:
   509→            continue
   510→        lines: list[str] = [f"### {dim}"]
   511→        for insight in insights:
   512→            if not isinstance(insight, dict):
   513→                continue
   514→            header = str(insight.get("header", "")).strip()
   515→            if not header:
   516→                continue
   517→            settled = insight.get("settled", False)
   518→            positive = insight.get("positive", False)
   519→            tags = []
   520→            if settled:
   521→                tags.append("settled")
   522→            if positive:
   523→                tags.append("+")
   524→            prefix = f"[{', '.join(tags)}] " if tags else ""
   525→            lines.append(f"- {prefix}{header}")
   526→        if len(lines) > 1:
   527→            sections.append("\n".join(lines))
   528→
   529→    if not sections:
   530→        return ""
   531→
   532→    header_block = (
   533→        "## Codebase Characteristics\n\n"
   534→        "Previous reviews established these characteristics. [+] marks positive\n"
   535→        "patterns; [settled] means confirmed. Augment this list: add new\n"
   536→        "observations, refine descriptions, settle or remove items as needed.\n"
   537→        "For full details, read `dimension_contexts.{dimension}.insights`.\n\n"
   538→    )
   539→    footer = (
   540→        "\nPrinciples: Keep your own context updates succinct. Each insight should have\n"
   541→        "a clear header (5-10 words) and a description explaining WHY, not WHAT.\n"
   542→        "Positive patterns get `positive: true`. Settle items when confident.\n\n"
   543→    )
   544→    return header_block + "\n\n".join(sections) + footer
   545→
   546→
   547→def render_scoring_frame() -> str:
   548→    return (
   549→        "YOUR TASK: Read the code for this batch's dimension. Judge "
   550→        "how well the codebase serves a developer from that perspective. The dimension "
   551→        "rubric above defines what good looks like. "
   552→        "Cite specific observations that explain your judgment.\n\n"
   553→    )
   554→
   555→
   556→def render_scan_evidence_note() -> str:
   557→    return (
   558→        "Mechanical scan evidence — navigation aid, not scoring evidence:\n"
   559→        "The blind packet contains `holistic_context.scan_evidence` with aggregated signals "
   560→        "from all mechanical detectors — including complexity hotspots, error hotspots, signal "
   561→        "density index, boundary violations, and systemic patterns. Use these as starting "
   562→        "points for where to look beyond the seed files.\n\n"
   563→    )
   564→
   565→
   566→def render_seed_files_block(context: PromptBatchContext) -> str:
   567→    return f"Seed files (start here):\n{context.seed_files_text}\n\n"
   568→
   569→
   570→def render_task_requirements(*, issues_cap: int, dim_set: set[str]) -> str:
   571→    dim_focus = render_dimension_focus(dim_set)
   572→    lines = [
   573→        "Phase 1 — Observe:",
   574→        "1. Read the blind packet's `system_prompt` — scoring rules and calibration.",
   575→        "2. Study the dimension rubric (description, look_for, skip).",
   576→        "3. Review the existing characteristics list — which are settled? Which are positive? What needs updating?",
   577→        "4. Start from seed files. Use scan evidence, historical issues, and mechanical findings as navigation aids.",
   578→        "5. Adjudicate mechanical concern signals (confirm/dismiss with fingerprint).",
   579→        "6. Augment the characteristics list via context_updates: positive patterns (positive: true), neutral characteristics, design insights.",
   580→        "7. Collect defects for issues[].",
   581→        "8. Respect scope controls: exclude files/directories marked by `exclude`, `suppress`, or non-production zone overrides.",
   582→        "9. Output a Phase 1 summary: list ALL characteristics for this dimension (existing + new, mark [+] for positive) and all defects collected. This is your consolidated reference for Phase 2.",
   583→        "",
   584→        "Phase 2 — Judge (after Phase 1 is complete):",
   585→        "10. Keep issues and scoring scoped to this batch's dimension.",
   586→        f"11. Return 0-{issues_cap} issues for this batch (empty array allowed).",
   587→    ]
   588→    next_num = 12
   589→    if dim_focus:
   590→        for focus_line in dim_focus.rstrip("\n").split("\n"):
   591→            lines.append(f"{next_num}. {focus_line.lstrip('0123456789abcdefghij. ')}")
   592→            next_num += 1
   593→    lines.append(
   594→        f"{next_num}. Complete `dimension_judgment`: write dimension_character "
   595→        "(synthesizing characteristics and defects) then score_rationale. "
   596→        "Set the score LAST."
   597→    )
   598→    next_num += 1
   599→    lines.append(
   600→        f"{next_num}. Output context_updates with your Phase 1 observations. "
   601→        "Use `add` with a clear header (5-10 words) and description (1-3 "
   602→        "sentences focused on WHY, not WHAT). Positive patterns get "
   603→        "`positive: true`. New insights can be `settled: true` when confident. "
   604→        "Use `settle` to promote existing unsettled insights. Use `remove` for "
   605→        "insights no longer true. Omit context_updates if no changes."
   606→    )
   607→    next_num += 1
   608→    lines.append(f"{next_num}. Do not edit repository files.")
   609→    next_num += 1
   610→    lines.append(f"{next_num}. Return ONLY valid JSON, no markdown fences.")
   611→    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"
   612→
   613→
   614→def render_scope_enums() -> str:
   615→    return (
   616→        "Scope enums:\n"
   617→        '- impact_scope: "local" | "module" | "subsystem" | "codebase"\n'
   618→        '- fix_scope: "single_edit" | "multi_file_refactor" | "architectural_change"\n\n'
   619→    )
   620→
   621→
   622→def join_non_empty_sections(*sections: str) -> str:
   623→    return "".join(section for section in sections if section)

   454→def _canonical_external_payload(
   455→    raw_payload: dict[str, Any],
   456→    *,
   457→    session: dict[str, Any],
   458→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   459→    """Return import payload with canonical provenance and required session token."""
   460→    session_meta = raw_payload.get("session")
   461→    if not isinstance(session_meta, dict):
   462→        raise CommandError(
   463→            "Error: external reviewer payload must include top-level `session` object."
   464→            ' Expected: {"session":{"id":"...","token":"..."},"assessments":{...},"issues":[...]}',
   465→        )
   466→
   467→    payload_id = str(session_meta.get("id", "")).strip()
   468→    payload_token = str(session_meta.get("token", "")).strip()
   469→    expected_id = str(session.get("session_id", "")).strip()
   470→    expected_token = str(session.get("token", "")).strip()
   471→    if payload_id != expected_id or payload_token != expected_token:
   472→        raise CommandError(
   473→            "Error: session id/token mismatch in external reviewer payload."
   474→            " Regenerate output using the session template/instructions.",
   475→        )
   476→
   477→    payload = {
   478→        key: value
   479→        for key, value in raw_payload.items()
   480→        if key not in {"session", "provenance"}
   481→    }
   482→    payload["provenance"] = {
   483→        "kind": "blind_review_batch_import",
   484→        "blind": True,
   485→        "runner": str(session.get("runner", "claude")),
   486→        "session_id": str(session.get("session_id", "")),
   487→        "created_at": _iso_seconds(_utc_now()),
   488→        "packet_path": str(session.get("blind_packet_path", "")),
   489→        "packet_sha256": str(session.get("packet_sha256", "")),
   490→    }
   491→    return payload
   492→
   493→
   494→def _ensure_session_open(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   495→    status = str(session.get("status", "open")).strip().lower()
   496→    if status == "open":
   497→        return
   498→    raise CommandError(
   499→        f"Error: session is not open (status={status or 'unknown'}). Start a new session with --external-start.",
   500→    )
   501→
   502→
   503→def _ensure_session_not_expired(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   504→    expires_at = _parse_iso(session.get("expires_at"))
   505→    if expires_at is None:
   506→        raise CommandError(
   507→            "Error: session metadata is missing/invalid expires_at.",
   508→        )
   509→    now = _utc_now()
   510→    if now <= expires_at:
   511→        return
   512→    raise CommandError(
   513→        f"Error: session expired at {session.get('expires_at')}. Start a new session with --external-start.",
   514→    )

    11→_NON_PRODUCTION_ZONES = frozenset({"test", "config", "generated", "vendor"})

    15→def collect_allowed_review_files(
    16→    files: list[str],
    17→    lang: object,
    18→    *,
    19→    base_path: Path | None = None,
    20→) -> set[str]:
    21→    """Return relative production-file paths allowed for holistic review batches."""
    22→    allowed: set[str] = set()
    23→    zone_map = getattr(lang, "zone_map", None)
    24→    resolved_base = base_path.resolve() if isinstance(base_path, Path) else None
    25→    for filepath in files:
    26→        if not isinstance(filepath, str):
    27→            continue
    28→        normalized = filepath.strip().replace("\\", "/")
    29→        if not normalized:
    30→            continue
    31→        if zone_map is not None:
    32→            zone_get = getattr(zone_map, "get", None)
    33→            zone = zone_get(filepath) if callable(zone_get) else None
    34→            zone_value = getattr(zone, "value", zone)
    35→            if zone_value is None:
    36→                zone_value = "production"
    37→            if not isinstance(zone_value, str):
    38→                zone_value = str(zone_value)
    39→            if zone_value in _NON_PRODUCTION_ZONES:
    40→                continue
    41→        allowed.add(normalized)
    42→        allowed.add(rel(filepath))
    43→        if resolved_base is not None:
    44→            try:
    45→                resolved_path = Path(filepath).resolve()
    46→            except OSError as exc:
    47→                logger.debug("Skipping invalid review file path %s: %s", filepath, exc)
    48→                continue
    49→            if resolved_path.is_relative_to(resolved_base):
    50→                allowed.add(resolved_path.relative_to(resolved_base).as_posix())

    54→def file_in_allowed_scope(filepath: object, allowed_files: set[str]) -> bool:
    55→    """True when *filepath* resolves to a currently in-scope review file."""
    56→    if not isinstance(filepath, str):

    61→    if normalized in allowed_files:

    43→    """Collect unique file paths from multiple source lists."""

    45→    out: list[str] = []
    46→    for src in sources:
    47→        for item in src:
    48→            fpath = _normalize_file_path(item.get(key, ""))
    49→            if fpath and fpath not in seen:
    50→                seen.add(fpath)
    51→                out.append(fpath)
    52→                if max_files is not None and len(out) >= max_files:
    53→                    return out
    54→    return out
    55→
    56→
    57→def _collect_files_from_batches(
    58→    batches: list[dict],
    59→    *,
    60→    max_files: int | None = None,
    61→) -> list[str]:
    62→    """Collect unique file paths across batch payloads (preserving order)."""
    63→    seen: set[str] = set()
    64→    out: list[str] = []
    65→    for batch in batches:
    66→        for filepath in batch.get("files_to_read", []):
    67→            normalized = _normalize_file_path(filepath)
    68→            if not normalized or normalized in seen:
    69→                continue
    70→            seen.add(normalized)
    71→            out.append(normalized)
    72→            if max_files is not None and len(out) >= max_files:
    73→                return out
    74→    return out
    75→
    76→
    77→def _representative_files_for_directory(
    78→    ctx: HolisticContext,
    79→    directory: str,
    80→    *,
    81→    max_files: int = 3,
    82→) -> list[str]:
    83→    """Map a directory-level signal to representative file paths."""
    84→    if not isinstance(directory, str) or not directory.strip():
    85→        return []
    86→
    87→    dir_key = directory.strip()
    88→    if dir_key in {".", "./"}:
    89→        normalized_dir = "."
    90→    else:
    91→        normalized_dir = f"{dir_key.rstrip('/')}/"
    92→
    93→    profiles = ctx.structure.get("directory_profiles", {})
    94→    profile = profiles.get(normalized_dir)
    95→    if not isinstance(profile, dict):
    96→        return []
    97→
    98→    out: list[str] = []
    99→    for filename in profile.get("files", []):
   100→        if not isinstance(filename, str) or not filename:
   101→            continue
   102→        filepath = (
   103→            filename
   104→            if normalized_dir == "."
   105→            else f"{normalized_dir.rstrip('/')}/{filename}"
   106→        )
   107→        normalized = _normalize_file_path(filepath)
   108→        if not normalized or normalized in out:
   109→            continue
   110→        out.append(normalized)
   111→        if len(out) >= max_files:
   112→            break
   113→    return out
   114→
   115→
   116→def _ensure_holistic_context(holistic_ctx: HolisticContext | dict) -> HolisticContext:
   117→    """Coerce raw dict payloads into a ``HolisticContext`` model."""
   118→    if isinstance(holistic_ctx, HolisticContext):
   119→        return holistic_ctx
   120→    return HolisticContext.from_raw(holistic_ctx)
   121→
   122→
   123→__all__ = [
   124→    "_collect_files_from_batches",
   125→    "_collect_unique_files",
   126→    "_ensure_holistic_context",
   127→    "_normalize_file_path",
   128→    "_representative_files_for_directory",
   129→]
   130→

    15→def _count_findings_for_dimensions(
    16→    state: dict,
    17→    dimensions: list[str],
    18→) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[str, int]]:
    19→    """Count open findings for detectors relevant to the given dimensions.
    20→
    21→    Returns (judgment_counts, mechanical_counts) keyed by detector name.
    22→    """
    23→    from desloppify.base.registry import JUDGMENT_DETECTORS, dimension_to_detectors
    24→
    25→    dim_detectors = dimension_to_detectors()
    26→    relevant: set[str] = set()
    27→    for dim in dimensions:
    28→        relevant.update(dim_detectors.get(dim, ()))
    29→    if not relevant:
    30→        return {}, {}
    31→
    32→    issues = state.get("issues")
    33→    if not isinstance(issues, dict):
    34→        return {}, {}
    35→
    36→    judgment: dict[str, int] = {}
    37→    mechanical: dict[str, int] = {}
    38→    for issue in issues.values():
    39→        if not isinstance(issue, dict):
    40→            continue
    41→        status = str(issue.get("status", "")).strip()
    42→        if status not in ("open", "reopened"):
    43→            continue
    44→        detector = str(issue.get("detector", "")).strip()
    45→        if detector not in relevant:
    46→            continue
    47→        target = judgment if detector in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS else mechanical
    48→        target[detector] = target.get(detector, 0) + 1
    49→
    50→    return judgment, mechanical
    51→

    53→def build_investigation_batches(
    54→    holistic_ctx,

    65→
    66→    file_cache: dict[str, list[str]] = {}

    70→        if collector_key not in file_cache:
    71→            collector = _FILE_COLLECTORS[collector_key]
    72→            file_cache[collector_key] = collector(
    73→                ctx,
    74→                max_files=max_files_per_batch,
    75→            )
    76→
    77→        files = file_cache[collector_key]
    78→        if not files:

    80→
    81→        batch: dict[str, object] = {
    82→            "name": dimension,
    83→            "dimensions": [dimension],
    84→            "files_to_read": files,
    85→            "why": f"seed files for {dimension} review",
    86→        }
    87→
    88→        if state is not None:
    89→            j_counts, m_counts = _count_findings_for_dimensions(state, [dimension])
    90→            if j_counts:
    91→                batch["judgment_finding_counts"] = j_counts
    92→            if m_counts:
    93→                batch["mechanical_finding_counts"] = m_counts

    95→        batches.append(batch)

    97→    return batches

    99→
   100→def filter_batches_to_dimensions(
   101→    batches: list[dict],
   102→    dimensions: list[str],
   103→    *,
   104→    fallback_max_files: int | None = 80,
   105→) -> list[dict]:
   106→    """Keep only batches whose dimension is in the active set."""
   107→    selected = [dimension for dimension in dimensions if isinstance(dimension, str) and dimension]
   108→    if not selected:
   109→        return []
   110→    selected_set = set(selected)
   111→    filtered: list[dict] = []
   112→    covered: set[str] = set()
   113→    for batch in batches:
   114→        batch_dims = [dim for dim in batch.get("dimensions", []) if dim in selected_set]
   115→        if not batch_dims:
   116→            continue
   117→        filtered.append({**batch, "dimensions": batch_dims})
   118→        covered.update(batch_dims)
   119→
   120→    missing = [dim for dim in selected if dim not in covered]
   121→    if not missing:
   122→        return filtered
   123→
   124→    max_files = fallback_max_files if isinstance(fallback_max_files, int) else None
   125→    if isinstance(max_files, int) and max_files <= 0:
   126→        max_files = None
   127→    fallback_files = _collect_files_from_batches(
   128→        filtered or batches,
   129→        max_files=max_files,
   130→    )
   131→    if not fallback_files:
   132→        return filtered
   133→
   134→    for dim in missing:
   135→        filtered.append(
   136→            {
   137→                "name": dim,
   138→                "dimensions": [dim],
   139→                "files_to_read": fallback_files,
   140→                "why": f"no direct batch mapping for {dim}; using representative files",
   141→            }
   142→        )
   143→    return filtered
   144→
   145→
   146→def batch_concerns(
   147→    concerns: list,
   148→    *,
   149→    max_files: int | None = None,
   150→    active_dimensions: list[str] | None = None,
   151→) -> dict | None:
   152→    """Build investigation batch from mechanical concern signals."""
   153→    del active_dimensions
   154→    if not concerns:
   155→        return None
   156→
   157→    types = sorted({concern.type for concern in concerns if concern.type})
   158→    why_parts = ["mechanical detectors identified structural patterns needing judgment"]
   159→    if types:
   160→        why_parts.append(f"concern types: {', '.join(types)}")
   161→
   162→    files: list[str] = []
   163→    seen: set[str] = set()
   164→    concern_signals: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   165→    for concern in concerns:
   166→        candidate = _normalize_file_path(getattr(concern, "file", ""))
   167→        if not candidate or candidate in seen:
   168→            continue
   169→        seen.add(candidate)
   170→        files.append(candidate)
   171→
   172→        evidence_raw = getattr(concern, "evidence", ())
   173→        evidence = [
   174→            str(entry).strip()
   175→            for entry in evidence_raw
   176→            if isinstance(entry, str) and entry.strip()
   177→        ][:4]
   178→        summary = str(getattr(concern, "summary", "")).strip()
   179→        question = str(getattr(concern, "question", "")).strip()
   180→        concern_type = str(getattr(concern, "type", "")).strip()
   181→        fingerprint = str(getattr(concern, "fingerprint", "")).strip()
   182→        source_issues = tuple(
   183→            str(sid)
   184→            for sid in getattr(concern, "source_issues", ())
   185→            if isinstance(sid, str) and sid
   186→        )
   187→        signal: dict[str, object] = {
   188→            "type": concern_type or "design_concern",
   189→            "file": candidate,
   190→            "summary": summary or "Mechanical concern requires subjective judgment",
   191→            "question": question or "Is this pattern intentional or debt?",
   192→            "evidence": evidence,
   193→        }
   194→        if fingerprint:
   195→            signal["fingerprint"] = fingerprint
   196→        if source_issues:
   197→            signal["finding_ids"] = list(source_issues)
   198→        concern_signals.append(signal)
   199→
   200→    total_candidate_files = len(files)
   201→    if (
   202→        max_files is not None
   203→        and isinstance(max_files, int)
   204→        and max_files > 0
   205→        and total_candidate_files > max_files
   206→    ):
   207→        files = files[:max_files]
   208→        why_parts.append(
   209→            f"truncated to {max_files} files from {total_candidate_files} candidates"
   210→        )
   211→
   212→    # Build per-detector judgment finding counts by extracting the detector name
   213→    # from each source issue ID (format: "detector::file::detail").
   214→    detector_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   215→    seen_source_ids: set[str] = set()
   216→    for concern in concerns:
   217→        for sid in getattr(concern, "source_issues", ()):
   218→            sid_str = str(sid)
   219→            if sid_str in seen_source_ids:
   220→                continue
   221→            seen_source_ids.add(sid_str)
   222→            detector = sid_str.split("::", 1)[0] if "::" in sid_str else ""
   223→            if detector:
   224→                detector_counts[detector] = detector_counts.get(detector, 0) + 1
   225→
   226→    result: dict[str, object] = {
   227→        "name": "design_coherence",
   228→        "dimensions": ["design_coherence"],
   229→        "files_to_read": files,
   230→        "why": "; ".join(why_parts),
   231→        "total_candidate_files": total_candidate_files,
   232→        "concern_signals": concern_signals,
   233→        "concern_signal_count": len(concern_signals),
   234→    }
   235→    if detector_counts:
   236→        result["judgment_finding_counts"] = detector_counts
   237→    return result
   238→
   239→

   241→    "batch_concerns",
   242→    "build_investigation_batches",
   243→    "filter_batches_to_dimensions",
   244→]

   268→        )
   269→        return
   270→
   271→    preview = ", ".join(missing_dims[:5])
   272→    if len(missing_dims) > 5:
   273→        preview = f"{preview}, +{len(missing_dims) - 5} more"
   274→    print(colorize_fn(f"  Missing dimensions: {preview}", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
   275→    print(

   278→            f"{TRUSTED_IMPORT_COVERAGE_OVERRIDE_FLAG}.",

   281→        file=sys.stderr,
   282→    )
   283→    print(

   287→            "dim",
   288→        ),
   289→        file=sys.stderr,
   290→    )
   291→    raise CommandError(
   292→        "Error: trusted assessment import blocked due to incomplete selected-dimension coverage.",
   293→        exit_code=1,
   294→    )
   295→

     2→

    17→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    18→class HolisticBatchAssemblyDependencies:
    19→    """Injected collaborators for holistic batch assembly."""
    20→
    21→    build_investigation_batches_fn: object
    22→    batch_concerns_fn: object

    29→def _merge_batch_payload(
    30→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],
    31→    incoming_batch: dict[str, Any],
    32→) -> None:
    33→    """Merge concern payload into an existing dimension batch when available."""
    34→    incoming_dimensions = incoming_batch.get("dimensions")
    35→    for existing in batches:
    36→        if existing.get("dimensions") != incoming_dimensions:
    37→            continue
    38→        existing_files = set(existing.get("files_to_read", []))
    39→        for filepath in incoming_batch.get("files_to_read", []):
    40→            if filepath in existing_files:
    41→                continue
    42→            existing["files_to_read"].append(filepath)
    43→            existing_files.add(filepath)
    44→        existing["concern_signals"] = incoming_batch.get("concern_signals", [])
    45→        existing["concern_signal_count"] = incoming_batch.get("concern_signal_count", 0)
    46→        judgment_counts = incoming_batch.get("judgment_finding_counts")
    47→        if judgment_counts:
    48→            existing["judgment_finding_counts"] = judgment_counts
    49→        return
    50→    batches.append(incoming_batch)
    51→
    52→
    53→def _append_concerns_batch(
    54→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],

    10→    zone_in,

    12→
    13→HOLISTIC_WORKFLOW = [
    14→    "Read .desloppify/query.json for context, excerpts, and investigation batches",
    15→    "For each batch: start from listed seed files, then explore likely hotspots/unreviewed neighbors; evaluate the batch's dimension (each batch covers exactly one dimension; batches are independent — parallelize)",
    16→    "Cross-reference issues with the sibling_behavior and convention data",
    17→    "IMPORTANT: issues must be defects only — never positive observations. High scores capture quality; issues capture problems.",
    18→    "Write ALL issues to issues.json — do NOT fix code before importing. Import creates tracked state entries that let desloppify correlate fixes to issues.",
    19→    "Codex: desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import",
    20→    "Claude / other agent: desloppify review --run-batches --dry-run → launch one subagent per prompt file (all in parallel) → desloppify review --import-run <run-dir> --scan-after-import",
    21→    "Cloud/external: run `desloppify review --external-start --external-runner claude`, follow the session template, then run the printed `--external-submit` command",
    22→    "Fallback path: `desloppify review --import issues.json` (issues only). Use manual override only for emergency/provisional imports.",
    23→    "AFTER importing: run `desloppify show review --status open` to see the work queue, then fix each issue in code and `desloppify plan resolve <id>`",
    24→]
    25→
    26→
    27→def append_full_sweep_batch(
    28→    *,
    29→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],
    30→    dims: list[str],
    31→    all_files: list[str],
    32→    lang: Any,
    33→    max_files: int | None = None,
    34→) -> None:
    35→    """Append an optional cross-cutting full-codebase batch."""
    36→    if not dims:
    37→        return
    38→    all_rel_files: list[str] = []
    39→    for filepath in all_files:
    40→        if lang.zone_map is not None:
    41→            zone = lang.zone_map.get(filepath)
    42→            if zone_in(zone, REVIEW_SELECTION_EXCLUDED_ZONES):
    43→                continue
    44→        all_rel_files.append(rel(filepath))
    45→        if isinstance(max_files, int) and max_files > 0 and len(all_rel_files) >= max_files:
    46→            break
    47→    if not all_rel_files:
    48→        return
    49→    batches.append(
    50→        {
    51→            "name": "Full Codebase Sweep",
    52→            "dimensions": list(dims),
    53→            "files_to_read": all_rel_files,
    54→            "why": "thorough default: evaluate cross-cutting quality across all production files",
    55→        }
    56→    )

   128→def process_unused_import_lines(
   129→    lines: list[str],
   130→    unused_symbols: set[str],
   131→    unused_by_line: dict[int, list[str]],
   132→) -> tuple[list[str], set[str]]:
   133→    """Process TS lines and remove/import-trim unused import statements."""
   134→    result: list[str] = []
   135→    removed_symbols: set[str] = set()
   136→    index = 0
   137→    while index < len(lines):
   138→        line = lines[index]
   139→        if not line.strip().startswith("import "):
   140→            result.append(line)
   141→            index += 1
   142→            continue
   143→
   144→        next_idx, replacement = _process_import_statement(
   145→            lines=lines,
   146→            start=index,
   147→            unused_symbols=unused_symbols,
   148→            unused_by_line=unused_by_line,
   149→            prior_output=result,
   150→        )
   151→        if replacement.removed_symbols:
   152→            removed_symbols.update(replacement.removed_symbols)
   153→        if replacement:
   154→            result.extend(replacement.lines)
   155→        index = next_idx
   156→    return result, removed_symbols

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.engine._scoring.policy.core import (
     6→    DETECTOR_SCORING_POLICIES,
     7→    DIMENSIONS,

    11→from desloppify.engine._scoring.results.health import compute_health_score
    12→
    13→
    14→def compute_score_impact(
    15→    dimension_scores: dict,
    16→    potentials: dict[str, int],
    17→    detector: str,
    18→    issues_to_fix: int,
    19→) -> float:
    20→    """Estimate score improvement from fixing N issues in a detector."""
    21→    target_dim = None
    22→    for dim in DIMENSIONS:
    23→        if detector in dim.detectors:
    24→            target_dim = dim
    25→            break
    26→    if target_dim is None or target_dim.name not in dimension_scores:
    27→        return 0.0
    28→
    29→    potential = potentials.get(detector, 0)
    30→    if potential <= 0:
    31→        return 0.0
    32→
    33→    dim_data = dimension_scores[target_dim.name]
    34→    old_score = compute_health_score(dimension_scores)
    35→
    36→    det_data = dim_data["detectors"].get(detector)
    37→    if not det_data:
    38→        return 0.0
    39→
    40→    old_weighted = det_data["weighted_failures"]
    41→    avg_weight = old_weighted / max(1, det_data["failing"])
    42→    new_weighted = max(0.0, old_weighted - issues_to_fix * avg_weight)
    43→
    44→    total_potential = 0
    45→    total_new_weighted_failures = 0.0
    46→    for det in target_dim.detectors:
    47→        det_values = dim_data["detectors"].get(det)
    48→        if not det_values:
    49→            continue
    50→        total_potential += det_values["potential"]
    51→        if det == detector:

1→"""Top-level batch building APIs for holistic review preparation."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from .prepare_batches_collectors import _DIMENSION_FILE_MAPPING, _FILE_COLLECTORS
     8→from .prepare_batches_core import (
     9→    _collect_files_from_batches,
    10→    _ensure_holistic_context,
    11→    _normalize_file_path,
    12→)
    13→
    14→
    15→def _count_findings_for_dimensions(
    16→    state: dict,
    17→    dimensions: list[str],
    18→) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[str, int]]:
    19→    """Count open findings for detectors relevant to the given dimensions.
    20→
    21→    Returns (judgment_counts, mechanical_counts) keyed by detector name.
    22→    """
    23→    from desloppify.base.registry import JUDGMENT_DETECTORS, dimension_to_detectors
    24→
    25→    dim_detectors = dimension_to_detectors()
    26→    relevant: set[str] = set()
    27→    for dim in dimensions:
    28→        relevant.update(dim_detectors.get(dim, ()))
    29→    if not relevant:
    30→        return {}, {}
    31→
    32→    issues = state.get("issues")
    33→    if not isinstance(issues, dict):
    34→        return {}, {}
    35→
    36→    judgment: dict[str, int] = {}
    37→    mechanical: dict[str, int] = {}
    38→    for issue in issues.values():
    39→        if not isinstance(issue, dict):
    40→            continue
    41→        status = str(issue.get("status", "")).strip()
    42→        if status not in ("open", "reopened"):
    43→            continue
    44→        detector = str(issue.get("detector", "")).strip()
    45→        if detector not in relevant:
    46→            continue
    47→        target = judgment if detector in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS else mechanical
    48→        target[detector] = target.get(detector, 0) + 1
    49→
    50→    return judgment, mechanical
    51→
    52→
    53→def build_investigation_batches(
    54→    holistic_ctx,
    55→    lang: object,
    56→    *,
    57→    repo_root: Path | None = None,
    58→    max_files_per_batch: int | None = None,
    59→    state: dict | None = None,
    60→) -> list[dict]:
    61→    """Build one batch per dimension from holistic context."""
    62→    ctx = _ensure_holistic_context(holistic_ctx)
    63→    del lang
    64→    del repo_root
    65→
    66→    file_cache: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    67→    batches: list[dict] = []
    68→
    69→    for dimension, collector_key in _DIMENSION_FILE_MAPPING.items():
    70→        if collector_key not in file_cache:
    71→            collector = _FILE_COLLECTORS[collector_key]
    72→            file_cache[collector_key] = collector(
    73→                ctx,
    74→                max_files=max_files_per_batch,
    75→            )
    76→
    77→        files = file_cache[collector_key]
    78→        if not files:
    79→            continue
    80→
    81→        batch: dict[str, object] = {
    82→            "name": dimension,
    83→            "dimensions": [dimension],
    84→            "files_to_read": files,
    85→            "why": f"seed files for {dimension} review",
    86→        }
    87→
    88→        if state is not None:
    89→            j_counts, m_counts = _count_findings_for_dimensions(state, [dimension])
    90→            if j_counts:
    91→                batch["judgment_finding_counts"] = j_counts
    92→            if m_counts:
    93→                batch["mechanical_finding_counts"] = m_counts
    94→
    95→        batches.append(batch)
    96→
    97→    return batches
    98→
    99→
   100→def filter_batches_to_dimensions(
   101→    batches: list[dict],
   102→    dimensions: list[str],
   103→    *,
   104→    fallback_max_files: int | None = 80,
   105→) -> list[dict]:
   106→    """Keep only batches whose dimension is in the active set."""
   107→    selected = [dimension for dimension in dimensions if isinstance(dimension, str) and dimension]
   108→    if not selected:
   109→        return []
   110→    selected_set = set(selected)
   111→    filtered: list[dict] = []
   112→    covered: set[str] = set()
   113→    for batch in batches:
   114→        batch_dims = [dim for dim in batch.get("dimensions", []) if dim in selected_set]
   115→        if not batch_dims:
   116→            continue
   117→        filtered.append({**batch, "dimensions": batch_dims})
   118→        covered.update(batch_dims)
   119→
   120→    missing = [dim for dim in selected if dim not in covered]
   121→    if not missing:
   122→        return filtered
   123→
   124→    max_files = fallback_max_files if isinstance(fallback_max_files, int) else None
   125→    if isinstance(max_files, int) and max_files <= 0:
   126→        max_files = None
   127→    fallback_files = _collect_files_from_batches(
   128→        filtered or batches,
   129→        max_files=max_files,
   130→    )
   131→    if not fallback_files:
   132→        return filtered
   133→
   134→    for dim in missing:
   135→        filtered.append(
   136→            {
   137→                "name": dim,
   138→                "dimensions": [dim],
   139→                "files_to_read": fallback_files,
   140→                "why": f"no direct batch mapping for {dim}; using representative files",
   141→            }
   142→        )
   143→    return filtered
   144→
   145→
   146→def batch_concerns(
   147→    concerns: list,
   148→    *,
   149→    max_files: int | None = None,
   150→    active_dimensions: list[str] | None = None,
   151→) -> dict | None:
   152→    """Build investigation batch from mechanical concern signals."""
   153→    del active_dimensions
   154→    if not concerns:
   155→        return None
   156→
   157→    types = sorted({concern.type for concern in concerns if concern.type})
   158→    why_parts = ["mechanical detectors identified structural patterns needing judgment"]
   159→    if types:
   160→        why_parts.append(f"concern types: {', '.join(types)}")
   161→
   162→    files: list[str] = []
   163→    seen: set[str] = set()
   164→    concern_signals: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   165→    for concern in concerns:
   166→        candidate = _normalize_file_path(getattr(concern, "file", ""))
   167→        if not candidate or candidate in seen:
   168→            continue
   169→        seen.add(candidate)
   170→        files.append(candidate)
   171→
   172→        evidence_raw = getattr(concern, "evidence", ())
   173→        evidence = [
   174→            str(entry).strip()
   175→            for entry in evidence_raw
   176→            if isinstance(entry, str) and entry.strip()
   177→        ][:4]
   178→        summary = str(getattr(concern, "summary", "")).strip()
   179→        question = str(getattr(concern, "question", "")).strip()
   180→        concern_type = str(getattr(concern, "type", "")).strip()
   181→        fingerprint = str(getattr(concern, "fingerprint", "")).strip()
   182→        source_issues = tuple(
   183→            str(sid)
   184→            for sid in getattr(concern, "source_issues", ())
   185→            if isinstance(sid, str) and sid
   186→        )
   187→        signal: dict[str, object] = {
   188→            "type": concern_type or "design_concern",
   189→            "file": candidate,
   190→            "summary": summary or "Mechanical concern requires subjective judgment",
   191→            "question": question or "Is this pattern intentional or debt?",
   192→            "evidence": evidence,
   193→        }
   194→        if fingerprint:
   195→            signal["fingerprint"] = fingerprint
   196→        if source_issues:
   197→            signal["finding_ids"] = list(source_issues)
   198→        concern_signals.append(signal)
   199→
   200→    total_candidate_files = len(files)
   201→    if (
   202→        max_files is not None
   203→        and isinstance(max_files, int)
   204→        and max_files > 0
   205→        and total_candidate_files > max_files
   206→    ):
   207→        files = files[:max_files]
   208→        why_parts.append(
   209→            f"truncated to {max_files} files from {total_candidate_files} candidates"
   210→        )
   211→
   212→    # Build per-detector judgment finding counts by extracting the detector name
   213→    # from each source issue ID (format: "detector::file::detail").
   214→    detector_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   215→    seen_source_ids: set[str] = set()
   216→    for concern in concerns:
   217→        for sid in getattr(concern, "source_issues", ()):
   218→            sid_str = str(sid)
   219→            if sid_str in seen_source_ids:
   220→                continue
   221→            seen_source_ids.add(sid_str)
   222→            detector = sid_str.split("::", 1)[0] if "::" in sid_str else ""
   223→            if detector:
   224→                detector_counts[detector] = detector_counts.get(detector, 0) + 1
   225→
   226→    result: dict[str, object] = {
   227→        "name": "design_coherence",
   228→        "dimensions": ["design_coherence"],
   229→        "files_to_read": files,
   230→        "why": "; ".join(why_parts),
   231→        "total_candidate_files": total_candidate_files,
   232→        "concern_signals": concern_signals,
   233→        "concern_signal_count": len(concern_signals),
   234→    }
   235→    if detector_counts:
   236→        result["judgment_finding_counts"] = detector_counts
   237→    return result
   238→
   239→
   240→__all__ = [
   241→    "batch_concerns",
   242→    "build_investigation_batches",
   243→    "filter_batches_to_dimensions",
   244→]
   245→

    45→        existing["concern_signal_count"] = incoming_batch.get("concern_signal_count", 0)
    46→        judgment_counts = incoming_batch.get("judgment_finding_counts")
    47→        if judgment_counts:

    49→        return

    12→    resolve_review_packet_context,
    13→)
    14→from .runtime.setup import setup_lang_concrete

    16→
    17→def do_prepare(
    18→    args,
    19→    state,
    20→    lang,
    21→    _state_path,
    22→    *,
    23→    config: dict,
    24→) -> None:
    25→    """Prepare mode: holistic-only review packet in query.json."""
    26→    context = resolve_review_packet_context(args)
    27→    next_command = build_run_batches_next_command(context)
    28→
    29→    # Keep prepare and external-start on one packet-construction contract.
    30→    try:
    31→        data = build_review_packet_payload(
    32→            state=state,
    33→            lang=lang,
    34→            config=config,
    35→            context=context,
    36→            next_command=next_command,
    37→            setup_lang_fn=setup_lang_concrete,
    38→        )
    39→    except ValueError as exc:
    40→        msg = str(exc).strip()
    41→        if not msg:
    42→            msg = f"no files found at path '{context.path}'. Nothing to review."
    43→        scan_path = state.get("scan_path") if isinstance(state, dict) else None
    44→        if scan_path:
    45→            msg += (
    46→                f"\nHint: your last scan used --path {scan_path}. "
    47→                f"Try: desloppify review --prepare --path {scan_path}"
    48→            )
    49→        else:
    50→            msg += "\nHint: pass --path <dir> matching the path used during scan."
    51→        raise CommandError(msg, exit_code=1) from exc
    52→
    53→    write_query(data)
    54→    _print_prepare_summary(
    55→        data,
    56→        next_command=next_command,
    57→        retrospective=context.retrospective,
    58→    )

    44→        all_rel_files.append(rel(filepath))
    45→        if isinstance(max_files, int) and max_files > 0 and len(all_rel_files) >= max_files:

94→def filter_batches_to_file_scope(
    95→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],
    96→    *,
    97→    allowed_files: set[str],
    98→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    99→    """Strip out-of-scope files/signals from review batches."""
   100→    if not allowed_files:
   101→        return []
   102→
   103→    scoped_batches: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   104→    for raw_batch in batches:
   105→        if not isinstance(raw_batch, dict):
   106→            continue
   107→        batch = dict(raw_batch)

   110→            scoped_files = [
   111→                filepath
   112→                for filepath in files_to_read
   113→                if file_in_allowed_scope(filepath, allowed_files)
   114→            ]
   115→        else:
   116→            scoped_files = []
   117→        batch["files_to_read"] = scoped_files
   118→
   119→        concern_signals = batch.get("concern_signals", [])
   120→        if isinstance(concern_signals, list):
   121→            batch["concern_signals"] = [
   122→                signal
   123→                for signal in concern_signals
   124→                if isinstance(signal, dict)
   125→                and file_in_allowed_scope(signal.get("file", ""), allowed_files)
   126→            ]
   127→            if "concern_signal_count" in batch:
   128→                batch["concern_signal_count"] = len(batch["concern_signals"])
   129→
   130→        issue_focus = filter_issue_focus_to_scope(
   131→            batch.get("historical_issue_focus"),
   132→            allowed_files,
   133→        )
   134→        if issue_focus is not None:
   135→            batch["historical_issue_focus"] = issue_focus
   136→

   138→        has_signals = bool(batch.get("concern_signals"))
   139→        if has_seed_files or has_signals:

    55→    confidence = str(item.get("confidence", "low")).lower()

## PHASE 1 SUMMARY

### Characteristics

**[+] Strong verb vocabulary in function names.** The codebase uses specific, intent-revealing verbs consistently: `compute_`, `detect_`, `collect_`, `extract_`, `normalize_`, `resolve_`, `build_`, `validate_`, `render_`, `prepare_`. These form a clear vocabulary that communicates what each function does.

**[+] Consistent `_fn` suffix convention for callable parameters.** With 713+ uses across the codebase, `_fn` is a well-established, consistent convention for dependency injection of callable parameters (e.g., `has_triage_in_queue_fn`, `safe_write_text_fn`, `is_file_cache_enabled_fn`).

**[+] Domain-specific naming in the triage/plan subsystem.** Stage names, lifecycle concepts, and workflow terminology are consistent and descriptive: `TriageInput`, `StagePrerequisite`, `StageReadiness`, `TriageProgress`, `cascade_clear_dispositions`.

**[+] TypedDict models are well-named.** `StateModel`, `ScanDiff`, `ReviewImportEnvelope`, `BatchResult`, `HealthBreakdown`, `SkipEntry`, `Cluster`, `CommitRecord` — all communicate their data shape clearly.

**[+] Underscore-prefix convention for private packages.** `_state`, `_scoring`, `_plan`, `_work_queue`, `_concerns` under `engine/` clearly signal implementation-private boundaries.

**[+] Consistent `cmd_stage_` and `run_stage_` prefixes.** Command entry points use `cmd_stage_observe`, `run_stage_enrich`, `run_stage_sense_check` — clear separation of command layer from execution.

**[Neutral] `do_` prefix is an established convention for review command entry points.** Used for `do_import`, `do_prepare`, `do_merge`, `do_external_start`, `do_external_submit`, `do_run_batches`. While generic in isolation, this is a consistent convention within the review command module.

**[Neutral] `si` abbreviation for TriageInput.** Used across ~12 files in the triage subsystem. Borderline terse but consistent enough to be a local convention.

**[Neutral] `helpers.py` used as filename in 10 places.** Each is scoped to its parent package and contains focused utility functions rather than being a grab-bag.

**[Neutral] Long file names in parser support.** Files like `parser_groups_plan_impl_sections_triage_commit_scan.py` are verbose but accurately reflect the argparse hierarchy they build.

### Defects

**DEFECT 1: `is_py_facade` and `is_ts_facade` return `dict | None`, not `bool`.**
- Files: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/python/detectors/facade.py` (line 15), `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/detectors/facade.py` (line 11)
- The `is_` prefix strongly implies a boolean predicate, but these return a dict with metadata on success or None on failure. Better names: `extract_facade_info`, `detect_facade`, or `parse_facade_metadata`.
- Impact: A developer calling these functions would reasonably expect `bool` — the current name is misleading.

**DEFECT 2: Residual `finding` vocabulary in scoring/triage code.**
- Files: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_state/scoring.py` (lines 17, 27), `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/core.py` (line 67)
- The codebase has migrated from `finding` to `issue` (there's even a `normalize_legacy_findings_alias` function), but 3 function signatures still use `finding` as a parameter name. This is vocabulary divergence from the codebase norm.
- Impact: Minor confusion for readers — the dominant convention is `issue`.

**DEFECT 3: `process_unused_import_lines` uses generic verb.**
- File: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/fixers/import_rewrite.py` (line 128)
- `process` is a generic verb that doesn't reveal intent. The function strips/trims unused imports from lines. A name like `strip_unused_imports` or `remove_unused_import_symbols` would be more specific.
- Impact: Low — the docstring explains it, and the function lives in a focused module.

---

## PHASE 2 — JUDGE

### a) DIMENSION CHARACTER

The desloppify codebase demonstrates strong naming discipline across its 893+ non-test Python files. A developer navigating the code would find a well-established verb vocabulary (`compute_`, `detect_`, `collect_`, `extract_`, `normalize_`, `resolve_`, `build_`) that communicates function intent clearly, along with consistent conventions like the `_fn` suffix for callables and underscore-prefixed private packages. The few naming defects are isolated and minor — a couple of `is_` functions returning non-booleans and a handful of residual legacy term uses.

### b) SCORE RATIONALE

Against global anchors, this codebase sits solidly in the "strong but not flawless" range. The naming conventions are deliberately chosen and applied consistently across a large codebase, which is impressive. The defects found are few (3 concrete issues) and low-impact — the `is_` prefix mismatch in facade detection is the most meaningful, but it's limited to 2 functions. The vocabulary consistency around domain terms (triage stages, clusters, dimensions) is notably good.

    79→def _apply_persisted_exclusions(
    80→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    81→    config: Mapping[str, Any],
    82→) -> None:
    83→    """Merge CLI --exclude with persisted config.exclude and apply globally."""
    84→    cli_exclusions = getattr(args, "exclude", None) or []
    85→    persisted_raw = config.get("exclude", [])
    86→    persisted = (
    87→        [entry for entry in persisted_raw if isinstance(entry, str)]
    88→        if isinstance(persisted_raw, list)
    89→        else []
    90→    )
    91→    combined = list(cli_exclusions) + [e for e in persisted if e not in cli_exclusions]
    92→    if not combined:
    93→        return
    94→    set_exclusions(combined)
    95→    if cli_exclusions:
    96→        print(
    97→            colorize(f"  Excluding: {', '.join(combined)}", "dim"),
    98→            file=sys.stderr,
    99→        )
   100→        return
   101→    print(
   102→        colorize(
   103→            f"  Excluding (from config): {', '.join(combined)}", "dim"
   104→        ),
   105→        file=sys.stderr,
   106→    )
   107→
   108→
   109→def _project_root_from_state_path(state_path_value: str | Path | None) -> Path | None:
   110→    """Infer project root from an explicit state path under ``.desloppify``."""
   111→    if state_path_value in (None, ""):
   112→        return None
   113→    try:
   114→        state_file = Path(state_path_value).resolve()
   115→    except OSError:
   116→        return None
   117→    if state_file.parent.name != ".desloppify":
   118→        return None
   119→    if state_file.name == "state.json" or (
   120→        state_file.name.startswith("state-") and state_file.suffix == ".json"
   121→    ):
   122→        return state_file.parent.parent
   123→    return None
   124→
   125→
   126→def _resolve_default_path(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   127→    """Fill args.path from detected language or default source path.
   128→
   129→    For the review command, the last scan path (stored in state) is used as the
   130→    default so that ``desloppify review --prepare`` works on the same scope as
   131→    the preceding scan even when the project files are not under ``src/``.
   132→    """
   133→    if getattr(args, "path", None) is not None:
   134→        return
   135→    runtime_root = get_project_root()
   136→    if getattr(args, "command", None) == "review":
   137→        try:
   138→            state_file = state_path(args)
   139→            if state_file:
   140→                saved = load_state(state_file)
   141→                saved_path = saved.get("scan_path")
   142→                if saved_path:
   143→                    args.path = str((runtime_root / saved_path).resolve())
   144→                    return
   145→        except (OSError, KeyError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
   146→            log_best_effort_failure(logger, "resolve default review path from saved state", exc)
   147→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
   148→    args.path = str(
   149→        get_default_scan_path(
   150→            project_root=runtime_root,
   151→            default_src=lang.default_src if lang else None,
   152→        )
   153→    )
   154→
   155→
   156→def _load_shared_runtime(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   157→    """Load config/state and attach shared objects to parsed args."""
   158→    config = load_config()
   159→
   160→    state_file = state_path(args)
   161→    state = load_state(state_file)
   162→    _apply_persisted_exclusions(args, config)
   163→
   164→    args.runtime = CommandRuntime(config=config, state=state, state_path=state_file)
   165→
   166→
   167→def _looks_like_desloppify_checkout(root: Path) -> bool:
   168→    """Return True when *root* appears to be the desloppify source checkout."""
   169→    package_dir = root / "desloppify"
   170→    pyproject = root / "pyproject.toml"
   171→    if not package_dir.is_dir() or not (package_dir / "__init__.py").is_file():
   172→        return False
   173→    if not pyproject.is_file():
   174→        return False
   175→    try:
   176→        text = pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   177→    except OSError:
   178→        return False
   179→    return 'name = "desloppify"' in text or "name='desloppify'" in text
   180→
   181→
   182→def _running_installed_package_from_checkout(
   183→    *,
   184→    cwd_root: Path | None = None,
   185→    module_file: str | Path | None = None,
   186→) -> bool:
   187→    """Detect running an installed package while standing in a repo checkout."""
   188→    root = (cwd_root or get_project_root()).resolve()
   189→    if not _looks_like_desloppify_checkout(root):
   190→        return False
   191→    current_module = Path(module_file or __file__).resolve()
   192→    try:
   193→        current_module.relative_to(root)
   194→        return False
   195→    except ValueError:
   196→        return True
   197→
   198→
   199→def _warn_if_running_installed_package_from_checkout() -> None:
   200→    """Emit a warning when CLI resolution bypasses the current checkout."""
   201→    if not _running_installed_package_from_checkout():
   202→        return
   203→    root = get_project_root().resolve()
   204→    print(
   205→        colorize(
   206→            "  WARNING: running installed desloppify package while current directory "
   207→            "looks like the desloppify checkout.",
   208→            "yellow",
   209→        ),
   210→        file=sys.stderr,
   211→    )
   212→    print(
   213→        colorize(
   214→            f"  Current checkout: {root}",
   215→            "dim",
   216→        ),
   217→        file=sys.stderr,
   218→    )
   219→    print(
   220→        colorize(
   221→            "  Use `python -m desloppify ...` or `./.venv/bin/desloppify ...` here "
   222→            "to run the local checkout instead of the installed package.",
   223→            "dim",
   224→        ),
   225→        file=sys.stderr,
   226→    )
   227→
   228→
   229→def _resolve_handler(command: str) -> CommandHandler:
   230→    """Resolve a CLI command name to its typed handler callable."""
   231→    return get_command_handlers()[command]
   232→
   233→
   234→def _handle_help_command(
   235→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   236→    parser: argparse.ArgumentParser,
   237→) -> None:
   238→    """Handle explicit help command when present in parser config."""
   239→    topic = list(getattr(args, "topic", []) or [])
   240→    try:
   241→        parser.parse_args([*topic, "--help"])
   242→    except SystemExit:
   243→        return
   244→
   245→
   246→def main() -> None:
   247→    # Ensure Unicode output works on Windows terminals (cp1252 etc.)
   248→    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
   249→        if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure"):
   250→            try:
   251→                stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   252→            except (AttributeError, OSError):
   253→                logger.debug(
   254→                    "Skipping stream reconfigure for %s (not supported)",
   255→                    getattr(stream, "name", "<stream>"),
   256→                )
   257→
   258→    parser = create_parser()
   259→    args = parser.parse_args()
   260→    if not args.command:
   261→        parser.print_help()
   262→        return
   263→    if args.command == "help":
   264→        _handle_help_command(args, parser)
   265→        return
   266→
   267→    try:
   268→        with runtime_scope() as runtime:
   269→            inferred = _project_root_from_state_path(getattr(args, "state", None))
   270→            if inferred is not None:
   271→                runtime.project_root = inferred
   272→            _warn_if_running_installed_package_from_checkout()
   273→            _resolve_default_path(args)
   274→            _load_shared_runtime(args)
   275→
   276→            handler = _resolve_handler(args.command)
   277→            handler(args)
   278→    except CommandError as exc:
   279→        print(colorize(f"  {exc.message}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   280→        sys.exit(exc.exit_code)
   281→    except KeyboardInterrupt:
   282→        print("\nInterrupted.")
   283→        sys.exit(1)
   284→
   285→
   286→if __name__ == "__main__":
   287→    main()
   288→

1→"""Python facade detection helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import ast
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import count_lines
     9→from desloppify.languages._framework.facade_common import (
    10→    facade_tier_confidence,
    11→    detect_reexport_facades_common,
    12→)
    13→
    14→
    15→def is_py_facade(filepath: str) -> dict | None:
    16→    """Check if a Python file is a pure re-export facade."""
    17→    try:
    18→        content = Path(filepath).read_text()
    19→        tree = ast.parse(content, filename=filepath)
    20→    except (OSError, SyntaxError, UnicodeDecodeError):
    21→        return None
    22→
    23→    if not tree.body:
    24→        return None
    25→
    26→    imports_from: list[str] = []
    27→    for node in tree.body:
    28→        if isinstance(node, ast.Import | ast.ImportFrom):
    29→            if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
    30→                imports_from.append(node.module)
    31→            elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
    32→                for alias in node.names:
    33→                    imports_from.append(alias.name)
    34→        elif isinstance(node, ast.Expr) and isinstance(
    35→            node.value, ast.Constant | ast.JoinedStr
    36→        ):
    37→            continue
    38→        elif isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
    39→            if (
    40→                len(node.targets) == 1
    41→                and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
    42→                and node.targets[0].id == "__all__"
    43→            ):
    44→                continue
    45→            return None
    46→        else:
    47→            return None
    48→
    49→    if not imports_from:
    50→        return None
    51→
    52→    loc = len(content.splitlines())
    53→    return {"imports_from": imports_from, "loc": loc}
    54→
    55→
    56→def detect_reexport_facades(
    57→    graph: dict,
    58→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    59→    """Detect Python re-export facade files and directories."""
    60→    entries, total_checked = detect_reexport_facades_common(
    61→        graph,
    62→        is_facade_fn=is_py_facade,
    63→    )
    64→
    65→    facade_files = {e["file"] for e in entries}
    66→    _detect_facade_directories(graph, facade_files, entries)
    67→    return sorted(
    68→        entries, key=lambda e: (e["kind"], e["importers"], -e["loc"])
    69→    ), total_checked
    70→
    71→
    72→def _detect_facade_directories(
    73→    graph: dict,
    74→    facade_files: set[str],
    75→    entries: list[dict],
    76→):
    77→    """Detect Python package directories where all modules are facades."""
    78→    by_dir: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    79→    for filepath in graph:
    80→        parent = str(Path(filepath).parent)
    81→        by_dir.setdefault(parent, []).append(filepath)
    82→
    83→    for dirpath, files in by_dir.items():
    84→        init_file = str(Path(dirpath) / "__init__.py")
    85→        if init_file not in graph or init_file not in facade_files:
    86→            continue
    87→
    88→        non_init_files = [f for f in files if not f.endswith("__init__.py")]
    89→        if not non_init_files:
    90→            continue
    91→        if not all(f in facade_files for f in non_init_files):
    92→            continue
    93→
    94→        dir_importers = graph[init_file].get("importer_count", 0)
    95→        tier, confidence = facade_tier_confidence(dir_importers)
    96→        total_loc = sum(count_lines(Path(f)) for f in files if Path(f).exists())
    97→
    98→        entries.append(
    99→            {
   100→                "file": dirpath,
   101→                "loc": total_loc,
   102→                "importers": dir_importers,
   103→                "imports_from": [],
   104→                "kind": "directory",
   105→                "file_count": len(files),
   106→                "tier": tier,
   107→                "confidence": confidence,
   108→            }
   109→        )
   110→

1→"""TypeScript facade detection helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import re
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→
     8→from desloppify.languages._framework.facade_common import detect_reexport_facades_common
     9→
    10→
    11→def is_ts_facade(filepath: str) -> dict | None:
    12→    """Check if a TypeScript file is a pure re-export facade."""
    13→    try:
    14→        content = Path(filepath).read_text()
    15→        lines = content.splitlines()
    16→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
    17→        return None
    18→
    19→    if not lines:
    20→        return None
    21→
    22→    imports_from: list[str] = []
    23→    export_re = re.compile(r"""^export\s+(?:\{[^}]*\}|\*)\s+from\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]""")
    24→    reexport_re = re.compile(
    25→        r"""^export\s+(?:type\s+)?\{[^}]*\}\s+from\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]"""
    26→    )
    27→
    28→    for line in lines:
    29→        stripped = line.strip()
    30→        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("//") or stripped.startswith("/*"):
    31→            continue
    32→
    33→        m = export_re.match(stripped) or reexport_re.match(stripped)
    34→        if m:
    35→            imports_from.append(m.group(1))
    36→            continue
    37→
    38→        return None
    39→
    40→    if not imports_from:
    41→        return None
    42→
    43→    return {"imports_from": imports_from, "loc": len(lines)}
    44→
    45→
    46→def detect_reexport_facades(
    47→    graph: dict,
    48→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    49→    """Detect TypeScript re-export facade files."""
    50→    entries, total_checked = detect_reexport_facades_common(
    51→        graph,
    52→        is_facade_fn=is_ts_facade,
    53→    )
    54→
    55→    return sorted(
    56→        entries, key=lambda e: (e["kind"], e["importers"], -e["loc"])
    57→    ), total_checked
    58→

Good findings. `is_py_facade` and `is_ts_facade` return `dict | None`, not `bool`. This is a clear name/behavior mismatch — the `is_` prefix strongly implies a boolean return. These are used as facade detection functions and would be better named `detect_facade` or `parse_facade_info`.

120→    for ch in import_stmt:
   121→        if ch in " \t":

   128→def process_unused_import_lines(
   129→    lines: list[str],
   130→    unused_symbols: set[str],
   131→    unused_by_line: dict[int, list[str]],
   132→) -> tuple[list[str], set[str]]:
   133→    """Process TS lines and remove/import-trim unused import statements."""
   134→    result: list[str] = []
   135→    removed_symbols: set[str] = set()
   136→    index = 0
   137→    while index < len(lines):
   138→        line = lines[index]
   139→        if not line.strip().startswith("import "):
   140→            result.append(line)
   141→            index += 1
   142→            continue
   143→
   144→        next_idx, replacement = _process_import_statement(
   145→            lines=lines,
   146→            start=index,
   147→            unused_symbols=unused_symbols,
   148→            unused_by_line=unused_by_line,
   149→            prior_output=result,
   150→        )
   151→        if replacement.removed_symbols:
   152→            removed_symbols.update(replacement.removed_symbols)
   153→        if replacement:
   154→            result.extend(replacement.lines)
   155→        index = next_idx
   156→    return result, removed_symbols
   157→
   158→
   159→class _ImportReplacement:
   160→    """Container for optional import replacement lines and removed symbols."""
   161→
   162→    def __init__(self, lines: list[str], removed_symbols: set[str] | None = None):
   163→        self.lines = lines
   164→        self.removed_symbols = removed_symbols or set()

   166→    def __bool__(self):

    43→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
    44→        return True
    45→    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":

    47→        return bool(members) and all(

    55→    confidence = str(item.get("confidence", "low")).lower()

    58→        "medium": 0.7,

    60→    }

    67→def scope_matches(item: WorkQueueItem | dict[str, Any], scope: str | None) -> bool:

    69→    if not scope:
